name: Non-specific Autoimmune Cerebellar Ataxia Without Characteristic Antibodies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Criteria for Autoimmune Cerebellar Ataxia (Seronegative)

criteria.description: Progressive cerebellar ataxia with gait and limb incoordination
Evidence of autoimmune dysfunction such as elevated CSF IgG index or oligoclonal bands without characteristic antibodies
Exclusion of genetic, metabolic, infectious, toxic, and paraneoplastic causes
Clinical improvement or stabilization with immunomodulatory treatment
MRI evidence of cerebellar atrophy or T2 hyperintensities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive cerebellar ataxia, evidence of autoimmune dysfunction without characteristic antibodies, and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is challenging due to absence of specific autoantibodies; relies on clinical presentation and exclusion.

common.symptomName: Impaired coordination of fine motor tasks

common.notes: Often mild and secondary to cerebellar dysfunction
searchTerms: muscle weakness that worsens with use
weakness or pain in hands and feet
nerve damage symptoms in arms or legs
seeing or hearing things not real

laboratory: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) IgG index or presence of oligoclonal bands
Absence of characteristic paraneoplastic or autoimmune cerebellar antibodies
Mildly elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
imaging: MRI showing cerebellar atrophy predominantly in the vermis and hemispheres
Occasional T2 hyperintensities in cerebellar white matter
genetic: No known pathogenic mutations identified; genetic causes excluded
other: Positive response to immunotherapy (e.g., corticosteroids, IVIG) supports diagnosis
Normal or mildly abnormal nerve conduction studies

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of characteristic onconeural antibodies (e.g., anti-Yo, anti-Hu)
History or evidence of underlying malignancy
Presence of oligoclonal bands with characteristic clinical features

redFlags: New onset seizures or altered mental status
Evidence of systemic malignancy or paraneoplastic syndrome
references: Hadjivassiliou M, et al. Autoimmune cerebellar ataxia: clinical features and immunopathology. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 2017.
Mitoma H, et al. Autoimmune cerebellar ataxias: clinical diagnosis and treatment. Curr Neuropharmacol. 2019.
